label: At D1, dips after an unrewarded S2 visit (strongest after a1 rare), deeper late in episode.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * last_is('a1 S2 u') * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is('a2 S2 u') * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == S2) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 7 sits near 1 and the variation that matters is at D1, where it reads the outcome of the previous trial. It dips sharply after an unrewarded visit to S2: about -0.16 after a1->S2 (rare) unrewarded and about -0.07 after a2->S2 (common) unrewarded. It is slightly higher after rewarded trials. The S2-unrewarded dip grows with episode time, on top of the timing baseline that already falls late in the episode. Unrewarded S1 visits do not cause the dip. The free fit adds a further dip for two losses in a row and a small negative dependence on belief log-odds at GO/D1 (lower when the observer believes S1 is good), which is why it scores higher. GO and D2 barely vary. No future or model-output variables are used.

issues: The recorded short form is not the best one. It puts episode-time scaling only on the a2->S2 unrewarded term. Scaling all three D1 terms by ep_trial, '(phase == D1) * last_is('a1 S2 u') * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is('a2 S2 u') * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial', scores 0.591 on dev and 0.581 on test. The recorded form scores 0.529 on test, and the additive ceilings are 0.58 (observed) and 0.61 (all). So the dip after a1 rare unrewarded and the rise after reward both grow with episode time, not only the a2 S2 u dip.
The label says nothing about the slight rise after rewarded trials, yet this is one of the three short-form terms. A reader of the label alone could not predict it.
The claim that the a1-rare dip is the strongest checks out: residual -0.161 vs -0.072 after a2 S2 u. The claim that unrewarded S1 visits cause no drop also checks out: residual +0.016 / +0.027.

The explanation says GO and D2 barely vary, but this is not true late in the episode. In the misses worst windows (t96-99, a run of a1->S1 rewarded), GO drops to about 0.70 against a prediction of 0.94. 'GO after a1 S1 r' remains over-predicted by -0.026, which fits the belief_lo / late-GO effect in the free fit.

Remaining systematic error after the improved form: D1 after a1 S2 r is over-predicted (-0.033), so the rise after reward does not apply to rare rewarded S2 trials. D1 after an unrewarded S1 visit is under-predicted (+0.016 to +0.027). Both are small.

Nonlinear time shapes did worse than linear ep_trial on test: exp(ep_trial/10) scored 0.38, exp(ep_trial/20) 0.51, an ep_dec==9 indicator 0.23, and ep_dec 0.575. A linear time scaling is a fair description.
